subject: Log snapshot formats, sample sizing, and ISO/FedRAMP preflight questions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acmebank.com>, Michael Perez <michael.perez@fedgov.gov>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Log snapshot formats, sample sizing, and ISO/FedRAMP preflight questions

Hi Alice / Michael —

Thanks again for the intake call this morning. To make the evidence intake and the dry-run efficient, a few concrete clarifications from our side:

1) Preferred log snapshot format: do you accept gzip-compressed JSONL (timestamp + structured fields) or do you prefer parquet exports for bulk queries? If parquet is preferred, can you confirm schema stability (same field names across windows)?

2) Sample sizing for control families that rely on logging (authN/authZ, session management, key usage): we proposed a 7-day contiguous snapshot plus a 30-day rolling sample for retention checks. Is that sufficient for your auditor(s), or do you expect a full 90-day contiguous window for certain high-risk controls?

3) Access for extraction: can we request a short-lived read-only role to your S3 bucket (or equivalent) that provides object metadata + object-level paths? Alternatively we can accept signed exports. If you allow roles, what is the preferred IAM principal name pattern?

4) Timestamp fidelity: are your logs timezone-normalized (UTC) and do you include monotonic request IDs that tie across services? If not, please highlight any joins we should be aware of.

5) Deliverables for the dry-run: we'll send an extraction spec + QA checklist. Would you like the extraction spec as a PDF or a shared Google Doc (we can do both).

Attachments: sample-log-extract-specs.pdf (draft)

Action: can you confirm the above by EOD Wednesday and flag any auditor constraints we should factor into the extraction plan?

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Sr. Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acmebank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Michael Perez <michael.perez@fedgov.gov>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Log snapshot formats, sample sizing, and ISO/FedRAMP preflight questions

Soojin —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick responses from Acme Bank side:

1) Format: gzip JSONL is fine for ingestion into our tooling. Parquet is acceptable but we prefer JSONL for the dry-run (parquet for final bulk handoff).

2) Sample sizing: auditors typically ask for a 90-day contiguous window for cryptographic key usage and any admin console activity tied to production systems. For session/auth logs, 30-day contiguous + 90-day rolling lookback is usually acceptable. Please plan for the larger windows for the FedRAMP controls.

3) Access: we can create an AWS IAM role with read-only S3 list/get permissions scoped to a prefix. Principal format will be arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-dryrun-<org>. We will send the role ARN and the principal naming convention in a follow-up.

4) Timestamps: logs are UTC. We do include request_id in the header for most services but a few legacy services only have a session_id. We'll document join keys in the extraction spec.

5) Deliverables: Google Doc preferred for the extraction spec so we can comment inline. PDF for finalized versions.

Attaching a copy of our SIG/CAIQ intake pack (sig-caiq-initial.pdf) — high level only.

We can commit to creating the role and a 7-day test snapshot by Friday. For anything requiring 90 days we'll need a signed intake + scope confirmation (procurement/legal) before we generate the full extract.

Best,
Alice Turner
Lead InfoSec Manager — Acme Bank

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acmebank.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Log snapshot formats, sample sizing, and ISO/FedRAMP preflight questions

Thanks Alice — a couple of technical follow-ups from infra: 

- For the read-only role, we'll need s3:ListBucket + s3:GetObject on the specific prefix as you mentioned. Can you also include sts:AssumeRole for the principal arn you create so our automation can pull a short-lived token?

- For the 90-day extracts, do you provide server-side compression or should we expect compressed files delivered? If we need to run transfers, we prefer compressed (gzip) to reduce egress time.

- Field-level encryption: if any PII fields are redacted in your extracts, please annotate that in the manifest (we cannot reverse). We also need the hashing/salting algorithm if you do pseudonymization.

Proposed tech owner to coordinate: david.kim@redwood.ai (I will set up a temporary transfer bucket and coordinate checksum verification).

-David
David Kim
Infrastructure Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acmebank.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Log snapshot formats, sample sizing, and ISO/FedRAMP preflight questions

Team —

I pulled our evidence mapping and adjusted the timeline to show two parallel tracks: (A) dry-run (7-day snapshot + verification) — target this week; (B) full intake (30–90 day extracts) — target after scope sign-off. See attached evidence-mapping-v2.xlsx for the mapping to ISO 27001 Annex A / FedRAMP controls.

Logistics: 
- I will own the intake package and checkbox for auditor acceptance.
- Olga, can you confirm whether the external auditor accepts a hashed-identifier manifest in lieu of PII? Some third-party auditors accept this if we provide hashing details.
- Alice, if procurement needs a formal MSA addendum for the 90-day window please loop legal early — that will slow the timeline.

Attachments: evidence-mapping-v2.xlsx

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Principal, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acmebank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Log snapshot formats, sample sizing, and ISO/FedRAMP preflight questions

Thanks everyone — quick confirmation from my side: auditors we typically work with accept hashed identifiers (SHA-256) with salt metadata provided in the manifest. We should include the salt rotation policy and hashing command example in the manifest.

Next steps and owners: 
- Alice: send role ARN and initial 7-day snapshot by Friday (owner: Acme SecOps).
- David: stand up transfer bucket + checksum plan (owner: infra).
- Marissa: finalize evidence mapping and flag any controls requiring 90-day extracts (owner: compliance ops).
- Soojin: consolidate into Google Doc extraction spec and share commenters list (owner: compliance program).

I'll mark this ready for the dry-run once we have the role and the 7-day export. If procurement requests an MSA addendum for 90-day extracts, we'll pause full intake until sign-off.

Olga Petrov
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
